grade.stack_chosen: Node.js/TypeScript with ws, mounted inside the existing Express REST process; presence, invites and the FIFO match queue kept in process memory
ruled_out_recommended: Running the WebSocket gateway inside the existing REST API process
Presence and matchmaking state in each pod's memory with no shared bus
One big Node process holding all 50k connections
red_flags_hit: Ignoring deploys and pod restarts that drop sockets, and the reconnect storm that follows
Running the matchmaking loop on every gateway pod with no coordination, which causes duplicate or conflicting matches (it happens as soon as the deployment has more than one replica)
unsupported_claims: It says sticky routing to one pod would keep presence and matchmaking working across replicas. Sticky sessions only pin each client to a pod, so players on different pods still can't see each other's presence, receive invites or be matched together.
grade.notes: Staying on Node fits the team, and the agent openly said single-process state was the main scaling risk and that load testing was needed. Even so, it put the WebSocket gateway inside the REST API process with memory-only state and no shared bus, and it didn't cover reconnect storms, sizing, autoscaling, protecting Postgres or observability, so this build won't survive launch at 50k players.
